formats.name: Liberty Table
formats.about: A small table of up to five people who meet in person, at a cafe or a restaurant, to talk about the election and what is at stake.

formats.name: Watch party
formats.about: People who meet in person to watch a big night together, like a debate or the results coming in.

formats.name: Registration party
formats.about: People who meet in person and help each other get registered to vote before the deadline.

formats.name: Vote together
formats.about: People who meet up and go to the polls together, on election day or for early voting.

formats.name: Meet your representative
formats.about: A few people from the same district visit their representative's local office together, with three questions to ask.

formats.name: Candidate team
formats.about: People who meet to find someone to run for a local seat that had only one name on the ballot, and to help them get on it.

formats.name: Canvass
formats.about: Neighbors who knock on doors together to invite people to the next table and ask what matters to them. Never to tell anyone who to vote for.

formats.name: Rally
formats.about: A peaceful, lawful rally in a public place for something you stand for. Check with your city about a permit first.

formats.name: Study circle
formats.about: A small group that reads one chapter, or plays one of the site's tools, and argues it through.

host.name: Liberty Politics
host.bio: I'm Liberty, and I'm in the fight for liberty, at home and abroad. I read the bill before I tell you what's in it, and I keep score on every vote in Congress, so nobody gets to hide behind a speech. Post anything and I answer you myself, usually the same day. Catch me wrong with a source and I fix it in front of everyone. Speeches bore me. A roll call that contradicts one makes my day. My brother, Iran Uncensored, fights for a free Iran.

doors.title: Watch the show together
doors.say: The show is better with people in the room. Host a watch party and I'll get people to it.

doors.title: Play the Uprising Simulator together
doors.say: Run a city's uprising with friends, then argue the plan through. Host a study circle.

doors.title: Play the Conflict Simulator together
doors.say: Play it out with others and argue what comes next. Host a study circle.

doors.title: Who falls next? A Regime Board night
doors.say: Go through the board with others and make your calls together. Host a study circle.

doors.title: Compare our Liberty Scores
doors.say: Take it, then compare your scores over coffee. Host a Liberty Table.

doors.title: Visit {name} at their office
doors.say: Take three questions to their local office with others who care. Host a visit.

kits.name: Election night watch party
kits.pitch: Watch the results come in with people who care as much as you do.
kits.title: Election Night Watch Party
kits.line: We watch the results come in together. Bring a friend.
kits.about: On November 3 the House, a third of the Senate and dozens of governors are on the ballot. Don't watch it alone. We meet, we watch the results come in state by state, we cheer, we groan, and we talk about what it means for liberty. Bring a friend, and something to share.

drive.name: Tuesday, November 3
drive.title: Election night. Don't watch it alone.
drive.line: Host a watch party where you live, and I'll get people to it.

kits.name: Early voting together
kits.pitch: Each of us votes early, then we meet up for coffee.
kits.title: Early Voting, Then Coffee
kits.line: Each of us votes early, then coffee together. Everyone welcome.
kits.about: Many states let you vote early in person. We meet at a cafe, each of us goes to vote at our own early voting site, and we come back to the cafe after. The coffee is for everyone who comes, whether they voted or not. Nobody is told who to choose. No photo of a marked ballot, and none inside a polling place. Check your state's early voting days and sites on your county's election page first.

kits.name: A Liberty Table this weekend
kits.pitch: Four of you, one question, good coffee.
kits.title: Liberty Table
kits.line: Four of us, one question, good coffee. Come argue with us.
kits.about: A small table: up to five of us at a cafe. One question to start, like what is really at stake on November 3. No speeches and no experts, just people who care about liberty talking it through. First time? Come and listen.

kits.name: Visit your representative
kits.pitch: Three questions, one office, a few neighbors.
kits.title: Visit Our Representative's Office
kits.line: A few of us, three questions, one local office. Come along.
kits.about: Every member of Congress has offices back home, and the staff keep count of who walks in. A few of us go together with three short questions about what matters to us, ask them politely, and write down the answers. Call the office first and ask when they see visitors. Nobody needs to be an expert: bring your own questions, or take three from their page on the scorecard.

kits.name: Find a candidate for an empty race
kits.pitch: A seat nobody ran for. Let's find someone who will.
kits.title: Candidate Team: Fill an Empty Seat
kits.line: One seat nobody contested. We find someone who will run next time.
kits.about: Many local seats had only one name on the ballot. We meet, look at the seats near us on Unopposed, and work out who could run next time, what it takes to get on the ballot, and how we would help. Nobody is told who to vote for. Anyone who wants a real choice on the ballot is welcome.

kits.name: Knock on doors together
kits.pitch: Two hours, a few blocks, an invitation to the next table.
kits.title: Canvass Our Neighborhood
kits.line: We knock on doors in pairs and invite neighbors to the next table.
kits.about: We meet, split into pairs, and knock on doors for two hours. We never tell anyone who to vote for. We ask what matters to them, invite them to the next Liberty Table, and listen. Wear good shoes. We finish with coffee and compare notes.

kits.name: A peaceful rally
kits.pitch: Make it seen. Public, lawful, peaceful.
kits.title: Rally for Liberty
kits.line: A peaceful rally in a public place. Bring a sign and a friend.
kits.about: We meet in a public place, peacefully, with signs that say what we stand for. Check with your city whether a gathering this size needs a permit before you post it. No violence, nobody filmed up close without asking, and we leave the place cleaner than we found it.

kits.name: A study circle
kits.pitch: One chapter or one simulation, then argue it through.
kits.title: Study Circle
kits.line: One chapter or one simulation, then we argue it through.
kits.about: We pick one thing: a chapter of a book on liberty, a night on the Uprising Simulator, a round of the Regime Board. Everyone reads or plays it before. Then we meet and argue it through. No speeches and no experts. First time? Come and listen.
